exposure: Behavioral intervention with meal replacements during pregnancy
outcome: Proportion of women who returned to prepregnancy weight
cohort: The study included 264 pregnant women with overweight or obesity, enrolled at 13.7 weeks' gestation.
finding: A prenatal behavioral intervention with meal replacements that reduced pregnancy weight gain had no significant effect on 12-month postpartum weight retention or on the odds of achieving prepregnancy weight.
